newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's Finmeccanica hunts international alliances.
newsitem.headline: Italy's Finmeccanica hunts international alliances.

text.p: Italian state-controlled engineering group Finmeccanica on Thursday posted a hefty loss for 1996 after making special provisions in a bid to prepare the company for international alliances.
Finmeccanica, controlled by state holding IRI , said in a statement it made a loss of 540.4 billion lire ($324 million) last year after an extraordinary writedown of 575 billion lire.
The group, which is one of Italy's biggest industrial concerns, with aerospace, defence, transport and energy interests, made a 40.26 billion lire profit in 1995.
It said the provisions would cover future restructuring and investment plans for its defence and aeronautical divisions, and added that it was determined to press ahead with privatisation.
"The decision to bring forward the writedown stems from the need to proceed more decisively with the policy of alliances," Finmeccanica said in a statement.

Earlier this month, Finmeccanica said it had signed a memorandum of understanding with Britain's General Electric Co Plc (GEC) to study opportunities for collaboration between their respective defence sector companies.
Analysts said the talks might lead to a partnership of huge potential that could speed up the consolidation of Europe's splintered defence industry.

"Finmeccanica has to become swiftly and actively involved in these alliances," the company said on Thursday, adding that the size of its role in any such link-ups would be reflected by how profitable it was.
It predicted a quick return to the black in 1997.
"(The provisions) will enable a return to profitability, before any other extraordinary items, even of a significant nature from this year on," it said.
Finmeccanica said it made a consolidated pretax profit of 58.2 billion lire in 1996, before extraordinary items, against 96.8 billion the year before.
Turnover totalled 13.88 trillion lire last year from a previous 12.84 trillion, with orders at the end of December standing at 28.22 trillion lire, little changed from the same period in 1995.

The Italian group accounts for 70 percent of the domestic defence business. Its defence interests include aerospace and satellite division Alenia and helicopter maker Agusta. Through Alenia it is involved in numerous European aircraft projects, including a regional aircraft joint venture and Eurofighter.
Finmeccanica said mergers in the U.S. defence and aeronautics sectors meant that European companies would also have to join forces to compete against U.S. competitors.
"The two strategic objectives which Finmeccanica has to build its policies around are international alliances and privatisation," the statement said.

IRI holds some 60 percent of the group and Finmeccanica said last year it hoped to be privatised at some stage in 1997. That now seems almost impossible and no new sell-off timetable has been given. $1 = 1,669 lire
